title: iterate-plan reviewer output
description: Structured output from Codex reviewing a plan via the iterate-plan skill. Enforced by codex exec --output-schema. All five top-level array fields are required-but-may-be-empty.

verdict.description: APPROVE = ready for next phase; REVISE = load-bearing issue to fix; BLOCK = fundamental design problem.

findings.description: Substantive issues. Required field; may be empty if verdict=APPROVE with nothing to flag.

severity.description: HIGH = load-bearing, blocks APPROVE; MEDIUM = real issue, considered but not blocking; LOW = nit / polish.

description.description: Full text of the issue. Cite plan sections / lines when useful.

suggested_action.description: What Opus should consider doing. Describe intent, not wording — Opus writes the actual revision.

register_ref.description: Set to null in the common case (no match). (Strict structured-output mode requires the key to be present, so null stands in for the prior "omit entirely" contract; semantically null = untagged, unlike iterate-review's same-named field which demands a real value.) Set to a register id ONLY when this finding is independently actionable AND its behavior falls within a specific entry's recorded bound/recovery in the accepted-risks register (docs/risk-posture.md at HEAD, provided in the ACCEPTED RISKS block when the register resolved for this pass). Do not set this to merely reference a posture decision — if a finding only restates something the register already covers with no new evidence, don't file it at all. Do not set this if you are presenting evidence that the entry's bound or recovery path is false — that is a fresh finding, not a match, even if it concerns the same behavior. The editor validates every register_ref against the register at HEAD at fold time (step 7); an unknown, malformed, or non-matching ref is treated as untagged.

plan_corrections.description: Tactical non-controversial fixes (typos, broken refs, contradictions). Required; may be empty.

location.description: Section name or anchor (e.g., 'TL;DR para 2', 'Phase 0 deliverable bullet 3').

fix.description: What it should be, in abstract terms. Opus does the edit.

open_question_answers.description: Answers to questions Opus posed in the plan's 'Open questions for Codex pass N' section. One per question (or explicit 'no information'). Required; may be empty if no open questions.

answer.description: Codex's answer with reasoning. Multi-paragraph fine.

new_questions.description: Questions you want answered in the next pass, each classified by WHO CAN SETTLE IT. Required; may be empty. If you can answer a question yourself from the context you were given, answer it in a finding or an open_question_answer instead of filing it here.

settled_by.description: Who can settle this. 'resolvable_in_fold' = answerable from the FULL plan plus the repository — you may only have been given a slice of it, so the editor likely already has what you're missing. 'needs_lookup' = a fact exists that settles it, but reaching that fact requires something you cannot do (a network call, an API query, running a benchmark or command). 'needs_human' = no fact and no derivation settles it; it needs the author's preference, risk tolerance, cost appetite, or product judgment. WHEN UNSURE, CHOOSE 'needs_human' — wrongly labelling an author's decision as machine-resolvable invites a fabricated answer, which is far worse than an unnecessary escalation.

why.description: One line justifying the classification — e.g. which section you'd need, what lookup would settle it, or which judgment only the author can make. This exists so the label can be audited rather than trusted; a bare enum is easy to rubber-stamp.
